newsitem.title: EGYPT: Agip finds more oil in Gulf of Suez.
newsitem.headline: Agip finds more oil in Gulf of Suez.

text.p: Egypt's oil ministry said in a statement on Thursday that a new oil discovery was made in the Ashrafi Concession located in the southern Gulf of Suez.

The discovery, called Ashrafi SW-2, was made by IEOC Co Inc, the Egyptian arm of Italy's Agip SpA., which was acting on behalf of Agip, the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation and Marathon Oil Co, the statement said.
It said an exploratory well with a depth of 6,618 feet and yielded 3,490 barrels of 30-grade oil a day and 1.8 million cubic metres of gas a day.
Marathon said last August that it made a new discovery called Ashrafi SW-1X at the concession.
Marathon Oil Co has a 50 percent interest in a joint venture operated by IEOC. Marathon Oil is a part of the USX-Marathon Group, a unit of USX Corp.
The Ashrafi field, which began production in 1992, has produced about 30 million barrels of oil.
The field currently produces 20,000 barrels per day, Marathon noted in a statement last August.
